### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s).

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via sys_metadata_audit (symbol, a field of const object enObjects; a field of const object esESObjects; a field of const object jaJPObjects; a field of const object zhCNObjects))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-0.mdx`  _(via sys_metadata_audit (symbol, a field of const object enObjects; a field of const object esESObjects; a field of const object jaJPObjects; a field of const object zhCNObjects))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **144** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f2b6cf230b4cddd795b854b044bbcd95e37b6f55` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5bf6094fc142f20e373ba5aa0ec645152053a641` — the merge of head `84a283fe4f22129c9ff20d2c259454391edda7f3` into base `f2b6cf230b4cddd795b854b044bbcd95e37b6f55`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5bf6094fc142f20e373ba5aa0ec645152053a641 && git checkout 5bf6094fc142f20e373ba5aa0ec645152053a641
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f2b6cf230b4cddd795b854b044bbcd95e37b6f55 84a283fe4f22129c9ff20d2c259454391edda7f3 && git checkout -B drift-repro f2b6cf230b4cddd795b854b044bbcd95e37b6f55 && git merge --no-ff 84a283fe4f22129c9ff20d2c259454391edda7f3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f2b6cf230b4cddd795b854b044bbcd95e37b6f55
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f2b6cf230b4cddd795b854b044bbcd95e37b6f55` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `84a283fe4f22129c9ff20d2c259454391edda7f3`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.field-select-shorthand-keeps-written-value.ts + packages/spec/src/shared/identifiers.zod.ts (SystemIdentifierSchema), packages/metadata-core/src/objects/sys-metadata-audit.object.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (the lock_state writer at :19453 and reader at :12666), packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-protection.zod.ts (MetadataLockSchema), packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts (the audit response's lockState), packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts (createColumn) and packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/schema-drift.ts (diffManagedTable); plus the narrowing-face floor, every diff path outside the prose faces: packages/spec/src/data/field.test.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/objects/sys-metadata-audit-lock-state.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.select-shorthand-refusal.test.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/en.objects.generated.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/es-ES.objects.generated.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/ja-JP.objects.generated.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/zh-CN.objects.generated.ts, scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json; and .changeset/25013-select-shorthand-keeps-written-value.md, read as the prose face it is.

Inputs: card #25013 (body and all three comments: claim 6316146057, dispatch 6316248493, os-dev-report 6318297750); PR #25122 body, its 12-file list, and the net diff `origin/main...84a283fe4` (merge-base `f2b6cf230`, 12 files, +304/-36, read with `git diff` on the shared checkout); the check-runs on the head. Nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. The shorthand transform (`selectWithOptions`, field.zod.ts:3052-3058). The strip `.replace(/[^a-z0-9_]/g, '')` is gone; the transform is lower-case plus whitespace runs to `_`. Accept-set reading: a shorthand string loads now only if it loaded before (the old strip only ever deleted characters, so whatever passes `SystemIdentifierSchema` after the change passed it before), with one degenerate exception named in item 3. The hyphen class (`'no-overlay'`, `'user-agent-based'`) moves from "loads as a different value" to "refused at `options.N.value`, `invalid_format`, the SystemIdentifier message", and the refusal is the existing one: `field.test.ts` pins the shorthand's issues equal to the explicit `{ value: 'no-overlay' }` issues at FieldSchema, `ObjectSchema.create` throws at module load, and `saveMetaItem` answers 422 `INVALID_METADATA` at `fields.status.options.1.value` with nothing stored. **Right** — a pure narrowing of the loading set, no new error code, no parallel validator.

2. `SelectOptionSchema.value` / `SystemIdentifierSchema`. The diff of `packages/spec/src/shared/` and `packages/spec/src/kernel/` between `origin/main` and the head is empty, and the `SelectOptionSchema` block (field.zod.ts:350-362) is untouched; the regex stays `^[a-z][a-z0-9_.]*$` with the 2-character floor. **Right — byte-identical, as the claim fenced it.**

3. The dot case. `'v1.2'` declared `v12` and now declares `v1.2`, a valid identifier: a value change inside the loading set, not a refusal. It is stated — the changeset's FROM/TO ("A dot is now kept"), the ledger entry's `reason`, the PR's acceptance notes — and pinned (`field.test.ts`: `['in_progress', 'closed_won', 'v1.2']`). **Right, stated.** One edge the prose does not name, judged immaterial: a shorthand of one letter followed only by dots (`'a.'`) was refused before (the strip left `a`, under the 2-character floor) and loads now as `a.`. No published accept set grows — the explicit form `{ value: 'a.' }` always loaded — so it is not a widening the Clause-② line owes; recorded so nobody re-derives it.

4. The explicit-object branch (`{ ...o, value: o.value.toLowerCase() }`) is unchanged. Lower-casing is the documented transform, not a deletion, and the card's defect class is silent deletion. **Right to leave** (③ OQ1).

5. `lock_state`. The writer at `protocol.ts:19453` stores `entry.lockState ?? 'none'`, a `MetadataLock` (`none | no-overlay | no-delete | full`, `metadata-protection.zod.ts:50`); the reader at `:12666` casts the raw column to `MetadataLock | null`; the response schema at `api/protocol.zod.ts:1869` types it `MetadataLockSchema.nullable()`. None of the three moved. `Field.text({ maxLength: 255, readonly: true })` holds all four spellings; the old select declared `nooverlay` / `nodelete`, which no row ever held, and the new test pins exactly those two as the members a select option cannot declare. No row rewritten, no reader fallback. **Right.** Column shape, read off the driver rather than re-measured: `lock_state` sits on no index (`occurred_at` and `(type, name, occurred_at)`), so `createColumn`'s unkeyed text-family arm makes a FRESH table's column TEXT, while an EXISTING `varchar(255)` — the width the select column was created at; `packages/qa/dogfood/test/upgrade-harness/fixture-18.0.0/database.sql:601` shows it — diffs clean under `diffManagedTable`: with `maxLength: 255` the varchar-length branch sees `declared === col.maxLength` (or `emitterWouldVarchar` false when the mirror is threaded), and the #12121 unbounded-text branch requires no `maxLength` at all. The dev's three readings (no bound → `manual_widen_varchar_to_text`; 32 → `narrow_varchar`; 255 → zero) are what `schema-drift.ts:1220-1330` says they must be. **Right.** A nit, not a finding: the object comment says 255 "is the varchar(255) the select column was created as" — true of an upgraded database; a fresh one lands TEXT with the bound enforced at the write seam (`max_length` over the bounded string types). Both hold every value the writer writes.

6. Served metadata. `GET /api/v1/meta/object/sys_metadata_audit` serves `lock_state` as `type: 'text'`, `maxLength: 255`, no `options`, where it served `select` with four options. A public-surface change, declared and carried at `minor` on `@objectstack/metadata-core`. Not a widening at the write seam: the column was `readonly`, so option membership never bound a write (the card's own stated limit), and text with a 255 bound is at most as wide. **Right.**

7. Translations. The four `lock_state` option labels drop from all four bundles, regenerated by `check-i18n-bundles.mjs --write`; the Lint lanes that run that check are green on the head. **Right.** The acceptance note "never displayed" is over-broad: it holds for `nooverlay` / `nodelete`; the `none` / `full` keys did match stored rows, so a generic grid over `sys_metadata_audit` that rendered select labels showed `无` / `完全锁定` and now shows the raw value. The changeset states the drop plainly, which is the published statement; the note's sentence is prose, not a defect.

8. The ADR-0087 ledger entry `18.field-select-shorthand-keeps-written-value.ts`: a D3 structured TODO with no D2 conversion and no `conversionIds` — correct, since no stored artifact carries the shorthand (it runs in the author's TypeScript), and `migrations.test.ts`'s ruling-B pin runs from D2 to D3, not the reverse. Major 18 is the current spec major (18.0.0) with a `semantic:18` region in `registry.ts.template`; the registry is generated at build and never committed, and since #22485 `spec-changes.json` and the upgrade guide are generated witnesses, so no committed projection is owed in this diff. The entry's runtime strings carry ADR ids only, no tracker number. **Right.**

9. `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`: three rows for the new save-door test's fake engine, written by `check-engine-double-contract.mjs --write`; the double asserts its dispatch shape through `assertEngineFindOnePredicate` / `assertEngineUpdateDispatch` / `assertEngineDeleteDispatch` as the sibling harness does. **Right.**

10. In-tree producers. The dev's AST census (140 calls, 189 shorthand strings, 2 hits, both `lock_state`; positive control at `ba244f1^` finds the OAuth hit) is not re-runnable under this review's read-only shape. Corroboration read instead: Build Core and the Dogfood Regression Gate are green on the head (a hyphenated shorthand now throws at module load through `ObjectSchema.create`), and a single-line `git grep` over `Field.select([...])` literals at the head finds no hyphenated string outside comments. **Right, with that limit named.**

11. Widened anything published? No new export, no new error code, no schema or accept set widened; the only gain is the helper's output range now including dotted identifiers the explicit form always accepted. **Right.**

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/25013-select-shorthand-keeps-written-value.md`: `@objectstack/spec` minor, `@objectstack/metadata-core` minor, `@objectstack/platform-objects` patch. The summary is `fix(spec)!:`, the body carries the BREAKING banner, the FROM → TO mapping with the one-line fix (write the option explicitly, or declare the column `Field.text({ maxLength: 255 })`), the ADR-0087 marker `registered field-select-shorthand-keeps-written-value` in the comment form the gate prescribes, and the two line-initial declarations.
- Level under ruling A: the kind decides. `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` (a value refused) takes at least `minor` on a moved package — spec and metadata-core both move published source and both are `minor`; platform-objects' regenerated bundles ride `patch`; `major` stays refused in the launch window. `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` gains only a test file, so no changeset is owed there. `Check Changeset` on the head is green, the level axis' own verdict. **Matches the diff.**
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing: ...)` — identical on the claim, the PR body and the changeset; matches the diff (no published accept set widens; the shorthand's loading set narrows on the hyphen class; the dot case is a value change inside the set, stated in the body). `narrowed` beside the `(narrowing)` arm is the pair the gate expects — no contradiction. **Right.**
- `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` — the highest-breaking kind applies (`narrowed` over `semantic`: the dot case and the `lock_state` type change are semantic faces of the same diff). **Right.**
- ADR-0087 disposition: `registered` with the D3 entry above; `check:adr-0087-registration` runs in the green Lint lanes. `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` would contradict the changeset's own fix line. **Right.**

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flag — file surface beyond the claim. (a) The semantic ledger entry: owed by the ADR-0087 gate once the changeset carries a prescription; the claim's "stop on a breach and explain it in the report" was met by the report, and the addition is accepted here. (b) `engine-double-contract.pinned.json`: a generated artifact written by its own tool, inside the claim's generated-artifacts clause. **No breach.**
- Dev flag — `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED locally (dist missing): Build Core on the head is green. **Answered.**
- Dev flag — suites ran on `88440a148`, before the ledger entry and the merge: Test Core on the head is the carrier (the check-run reading below). **Answered by CI.**
- OQ1 (explicit `{ value: 'Active' }` still lower-cased): **A, keep.** Lower-casing is the documented transform and lands on an identifier the author can read back in the served options; `SelectOptionSchema.value` already refuses anything else. B is a second narrowing with no measured producer and outside this card's claim — a new card if anyone wants it, not this PR.
- OQ2 (`lock_state` as text, the closed set with `MetadataLockSchema` at the writer): **A, accept.** It is the claim's own cross-domain path; B needs a reader mapping or a `??` fallback (Prime Directive #12) or a row rewrite, all of which the ruling fenced out.
- OQ3 (`registered` + D3 entry versus `not-required`): **A.** The changeset prescribes a TypeScript-author rewrite, so `no-migration-prescription` would be false on substance; a D3 structured TODO is what ADR-0087 D3 is for when no artifact carries the shape.
- Out-of-scope finding 1 (the dot case, noted not filed): accepted — stated in FROM/TO and the ledger entry, pinned by test, no in-tree dot shorthand found. **No card owed.**
- Out-of-scope finding 2 (translated labels never displayed): accepted with the correction in ① item 7 (the `none` / `full` keys did match rows). The changeset states the drop. **No card owed.**
- The Docs Drift Check comment: two release-owned pages name `sys_metadata_audit` by symbol only; `git grep lock_state` over `content/docs` at the head is empty, so no page restates the option list. **Nothing owed.**
- Check-runs on the head, read at 2026-10-21T14:36Z: 41 runs — 31 success, 7 skipped (opt-in and path-filtered lanes), 3 in progress (Test Core 2/6, 3/6, 4/6). Green among them: Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates and every Lint lane, Build Core, Dogfood Regression Gate, Spec property liveness, Type Check · source gates / debt ledger / workspace / consumer gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core 1/6, 5/6 and 6/6, the card-claims-branch and single-writer checks. An earlier reading at 2026-10-21T14:28Z had Test Core 1-6/6, the two Type Check lanes and TypeScript Type Check still open; all but the three named have since completed green. Commit-status API: 0 statuses. This verdict is the contract reading; the landing still waits for every check green, which the queue guard holds on its own.

Implemented-by: `session_0123qkvzKLQfRRRnuR8wanHJ`
Reviewed-by: `session_01VsqhiSrBjB1wJfRNcHPeXN`

**VERDICT: PASS**
